tests.scenario: Verify the live application against Users can register using a manual registration form with the following fields: — Confirm Password: Required. Masked input. Error if empty: "Confirm the password".
steps: Open the application URL
Navigate to the relevant screen
Check whether the reported discrepancy is present in the live UI
tests.expected_result: The registration form only shows Name, Email, and Password fields; there is no Confirm Password field visible in the design.
tests.rc_reasoning: The Confirm Password field is critical to account registration as it protects users from password entry errors that would lock them out of their account, directly enabling the core workflow of account creation and subsequent order/wishlist/profile management.

tests.scenario: Verify the live application against The Password field includes a show/hide toggle icon that allows the user to reveal or conceal the masked input.
steps: Open the application URL
Navigate to the relevant screen
Check whether the reported discrepancy is present in the live UI
tests.expected_result: The Password field does not display any visible show/hide toggle icon on its right side.
tests.rc_reasoning: The show/hide password toggle enhances usability during account creation but is not central to the core business value — users can still successfully create an account and manage orders, wishlist, and profile without it, as password masking works by default without the toggle.

tests.scenario: Verify the live application against The sign up screen displays the Exclusive platform logo prominently, above the registration form.
steps: Open the application URL
Navigate to the relevant screen
Check whether the reported discrepancy is present in the live UI
tests.expected_result: There is no Exclusive logo visible above the registration form in the right panel; the logo only appears in the top navigation bar, not prominently above the form itself.
tests.rc_reasoning: Displaying the logo prominently above the registration form is a branding/UI aesthetic requirement that does not affect the core account creation workflow, user data protection, or the ability to manage orders, wishlist, and profile.

tests.scenario: Verify the live application against A visual divider or separator (e.g. a horizontal line with the label 'Or') is displayed between the Create Account button and the Sign up with Google button.
steps: Open the application URL
Navigate to the relevant screen
Check whether the reported discrepancy is present in the live UI
tests.expected_result: There is no horizontal line, 'Or' label, or any other visual divider visible between the Create Account button and the Sign up with Google button.
tests.rc_reasoning: The visual divider between the Create Account and Sign up with Google buttons is a minor UI/UX presentational detail that does not affect the core account creation workflow, user data protection, or the ability to complete registration through either method.

tests.scenario: Successful registration with a valid name entered in the Name field
steps: Navigate to the Exclusive platform registration page
Locate the Name field on the registration form
Enter a valid name, e.g., 'John Doe'
Fill in all other required fields with valid data
Click the 'Sign Up' or 'Register' button
tests.expected_result: The account is created successfully, no error message is displayed for the Name field, and the user is redirected to their account dashboard or a confirmation page

tests.scenario: Registration fails when the Name field is left empty
steps: Navigate to the Exclusive platform registration page
Leave the Name field completely blank
Fill in all other required fields with valid data
Click the 'Sign Up' or 'Register' button
tests.expected_result: Registration is blocked, the Name field is highlighted as invalid, and the error message 'Name is required' is displayed beneath or adjacent to the Name field

tests.scenario: Registration with a Name field containing exactly 1 character (minimum boundary)
steps: Navigate to the Exclusive platform registration page
Enter a single character in the Name field, e.g., 'A'
Fill in all other required fields with valid data
Click the 'Sign Up' or 'Register' button
tests.expected_result: If a single character is accepted as a valid name, the account is created successfully with no error shown; if the system enforces a minimum length greater than 1, an appropriate validation error is displayed instead of the generic 'Name is required' message

tests.scenario: Register with a valid email address in the manual registration form
steps: Navigate to the Exclusive platform registration page
Locate the Email field in the manual registration form
Enter a valid email address (e.g., 'john.doe@example.com')
Fill in all other required fields with valid data
Click the 'Sign Up' or 'Register' button
tests.expected_result: The form is submitted successfully without any email-related error messages, and the user account is created

tests.scenario: Register with an invalid email format and verify error message is displayed
steps: Navigate to the Exclusive platform registration page
Locate the Email field in the manual registration form
Enter an invalid email address (e.g., 'johndoe.com' or 'john@' or 'john doe@example')
Fill in all other required fields with valid data
Click the 'Sign Up' or 'Register' button
tests.expected_result: The form is not submitted and the error message 'Invalid email number' is displayed beneath or adjacent to the Email field

tests.scenario: Register with an email address at the maximum boundary length (254 characters as per RFC 5321)
steps: Navigate to the Exclusive platform registration page
Locate the Email field in the manual registration form
Enter an email address exactly 254 characters long with a valid format (e.g., a local part of 64 characters + '@' + a domain totalling 254 characters, such as 'aaaa...a@aaaa...a.com')
Fill in all other required fields with valid data
Click the 'Sign Up' or 'Register' button
Repeat the test entering an email address of 255 characters to test one character beyond the boundary
tests.expected_result: An email of exactly 254 characters is accepted and the account is created successfully; an email of 255 characters is rejected with an appropriate error message and the form is not submitted

tests.scenario: Register with a valid password in the password field
steps: Navigate to the Exclusive platform registration page
Locate the Password field
Enter a valid password (e.g., 'SecurePass123!')
Verify the input is masked (displayed as dots or asterisks)
Fill in all other required fields with valid data
Click the 'Sign Up' or 'Register' button
tests.expected_result: The password is accepted, input is visually masked throughout entry, no error message is displayed, and the user is successfully registered and redirected to their account dashboard or a confirmation page

tests.scenario: Attempt to register with the password field left empty
steps: Navigate to the Exclusive platform registration page
Fill in all required fields with valid data except the Password field
Leave the Password field completely empty
Click the 'Sign Up' or 'Register' button
tests.expected_result: Registration is blocked, the Password field is highlighted with a validation error, and the error message 'Password is required' is displayed beneath or adjacent to the Password field

tests.scenario: Register with a single-character password to test minimum boundary length
steps: Navigate to the Exclusive platform registration page
Locate the Password field
Enter a single character (e.g., 'A') as the password
Verify the single character is masked
Fill in all other required fields with valid data
Click the 'Sign Up' or 'Register' button
tests.expected_result: If the platform enforces a minimum password length greater than 1 character, a validation error is displayed indicating the minimum length requirement and registration is blocked; if no minimum length is enforced beyond non-empty, the password is accepted and the user is registered successfully

tests.scenario: Successfully register with a valid matching Confirm Password value
steps: Navigate to the Exclusive platform registration page
Fill in all required fields with valid data (First Name, Last Name, Email, Phone, Password)
Enter a valid password (e.g., 'SecurePass123!') in the Password field
Enter the same value ('SecurePass123!') in the Confirm Password field
Click the 'Create Account' button
tests.expected_result: The account is created successfully, the user is redirected to the account dashboard or a confirmation page, and no error is shown for the Confirm Password field

tests.scenario: Show error message when Confirm Password field is left empty on form submission
steps: Navigate to the Exclusive platform registration page
Fill in all required fields with valid data (First Name, Last Name, Email, Phone, Password)
Leave the Confirm Password field completely empty
Click the 'Create Account' button
tests.expected_result: Form submission is blocked and the error message 'Confirm the password' is displayed beneath or adjacent to the Confirm Password field

tests.scenario: Verify Confirm Password field masks input and accepts a single character as boundary minimum input
steps: Navigate to the Exclusive platform registration page
Click on the Confirm Password field
Type a single character (e.g., 'A') into the Confirm Password field
Observe whether the character is visually masked (displayed as a dot or asterisk)
Attempt to submit the form with only one character in the Confirm Password field while the Password field contains a longer value
tests.expected_result: The single character entered in the Confirm Password field is masked immediately upon input; the form should not submit successfully because the value does not match the Password field, and an appropriate mismatch or validation error is displayed

tests.scenario: Successful account creation with all valid fields and redirect to Home Screen
steps: Navigate to the Exclusive platform registration page
Enter a valid first name (e.g., 'Jane')
Enter a valid last name (e.g., 'Doe')
Enter a valid unique email address (e.g., 'jane.doe@example.com')
Enter a valid phone number (e.g., '+1234567890')
Enter a strong password that meets requirements (e.g., 'Test@1234')
Re-enter the same password in the confirm password field
Click the 'Create Account' button
tests.expected_result: All fields pass validation, the account is successfully created, and the user is redirected to the Home Screen

tests.scenario: Account creation fails when the email field is left empty
steps: Navigate to the Exclusive platform registration page
Enter a valid first name (e.g., 'Jane')
Enter a valid last name (e.g., 'Doe')
Leave the email field blank
Enter a valid phone number (e.g., '+1234567890')
Enter a valid password (e.g., 'Test@1234')
Re-enter the same password in the confirm password field
Click the 'Create Account' button
tests.expected_result: The form is not submitted, an inline validation error message is displayed on the email field (e.g., 'Email is required'), and the user remains on the registration page

tests.scenario: Account creation fails when password is exactly one character below the minimum required length
steps: Navigate to the Exclusive platform registration page
Enter a valid first name (e.g., 'Jane')
Enter a valid last name (e.g., 'Doe')
Enter a valid unique email address (e.g., 'jane.boundary@example.com')
Enter a valid phone number (e.g., '+1234567890')
Enter a password that is one character shorter than the minimum required length (e.g., if minimum is 8 characters, enter 'Test@12')
Re-enter the same 7-character password in the confirm password field
Click the 'Create Account' button
tests.expected_result: The form is not submitted, an inline validation error is displayed on the password field indicating the password does not meet the minimum length requirement, and the user remains on the registration page

tests.scenario: Successful Google OAuth 2.0 flow initiated when tapping Sign up with Google button
steps: Launch the Exclusive platform and navigate to the registration page
Locate the 'Sign up with Google' button on the registration page
Tap the 'Sign up with Google' button
Select a valid Google account from the Google account chooser popup
Grant the requested permissions on the Google OAuth consent screen
tests.expected_result: The Google OAuth 2.0 flow is successfully initiated, the user is authenticated via Google, a new Exclusive account is created and linked to the Google identity, and the user is redirected to their account dashboard with access to orders, wishlist, and profile

tests.scenario: Sign up with Google button is absent or non-functional on the registration page
steps: Launch the Exclusive platform and navigate to the registration page
Inspect the registration page for the presence of the 'Sign up with Google' button
If the button is present but disabled or broken, attempt to tap it
Observe the response after tapping the non-functional button
tests.expected_result: If the button is missing, a visible and accessible 'Sign up with Google' button must be present — its absence is a defect. If the button is present but non-functional, tapping it should display a meaningful error message such as 'Google sign-up is currently unavailable. Please try again later.' and no OAuth flow should be partially initiated

tests.scenario: User dismisses the Google OAuth consent screen mid-flow without granting permissions
steps: Launch the Exclusive platform and navigate to the registration page
Tap the 'Sign up with Google' button to initiate the Google OAuth 2.0 flow
When the Google account chooser or OAuth consent screen appears, tap 'Cancel' or close the popup without selecting an account or granting permissions
Observe the state of the Exclusive registration page after dismissal
tests.expected_result: The OAuth flow is safely aborted, no partial account is created, the user is returned to the Exclusive registration page in its original state, and an informational message such as 'Google sign-up was cancelled. Please try again or use another registration method.' is displayed without any application crash or data leakage

tests.scenario: Verify 'Log in' link is visible and redirects existing users to the login page
steps: Open the Exclusive platform in a web browser
Navigate to the account registration page
Scroll to the bottom of the registration form
Locate the 'Log in' link text at the bottom of the form
Click the 'Log in' link
tests.expected_result: The 'Log in' link is clearly visible at the bottom of the registration form and clicking it redirects the user to the login page, preventing duplicate account creation

tests.scenario: Verify registration form does not allow submission without the 'Log in' link being present as a navigation safeguard element
steps: Open the Exclusive platform in a web browser
Navigate to the account registration page
Inspect the bottom of the registration form for the 'Log in' link
Simulate or observe a scenario where the 'Log in' link is missing or not rendered (e.g., due to a UI rendering failure or broken element)
Attempt to complete and submit the registration form without the link being accessible
tests.expected_result: The 'Log in' link must always be present and rendered at the bottom of the form; if it is absent, this is flagged as a UI defect and the page should not be considered fully functional, as users have no visible path to avoid duplicate registration

tests.scenario: Verify 'Log in' link text matches exactly the specified label and is positioned at the very bottom boundary of the registration form
steps: Open the Exclusive platform in a web browser
Navigate to the account registration page
Scroll to the absolute bottom of the registration form
Inspect the link text to confirm it reads exactly 'Log in' (checking for case sensitivity, extra spaces, or alternate wording such as 'Login' or 'Sign in')
Verify the link is positioned after all other form fields and buttons, at the bottom boundary of the form
tests.expected_result: The link text reads exactly 'Log in' (matching the specified label precisely) and is located at the bottom of the form, not above any form fields or submit button, ensuring correct placement at the form's lower boundary

tests.scenario: Display error message when registering with an already registered email
steps: Navigate to the Exclusive platform registration page
Enter a first name, last name, and phone number in the respective fields
Enter an email address that is already associated with an existing account (e.g., existing_user@example.com)
Enter a valid password and confirm the password
Click the 'Sign Up' or 'Create Account' button
tests.expected_result: The system prevents account creation and displays the error message: 'An account with this email already exists' near the email field or at the top of the form

tests.scenario: No error message shown when registering with a brand new, never-used email
steps: Navigate to the Exclusive platform registration page
Enter a first name, last name, and phone number in the respective fields
Enter a unique email address that has never been registered (e.g., brand_new_user_12345@example.com)
Enter a valid password and confirm the password
Click the 'Sign Up' or 'Create Account' button
tests.expected_result: The system successfully creates the account, redirects the user to the appropriate page (e.g., home or profile), and does NOT display the message 'An account with this email already exists'

tests.scenario: Display error when registering with an already registered email that differs only in letter casing
steps: Ensure an account already exists for the email 'existing_user@example.com'
Navigate to the Exclusive platform registration page
Enter a first name, last name, and phone number in the respective fields
Enter the same email address using different casing (e.g., 'EXISTING_USER@EXAMPLE.COM' or 'Existing_User@Example.Com')
Enter a valid password and confirm the password
Click the 'Sign Up' or 'Create Account' button
tests.expected_result: The system treats the email as case-insensitive, prevents account creation, and displays the error message: 'An account with this email already exists'

tests.scenario: Exclusive platform logo is displayed prominently above the registration form on the sign up screen
steps: Open a supported web browser
Navigate to the Exclusive platform sign up URL
Observe the sign up screen layout once the page fully loads
tests.expected_result: The Exclusive platform logo is visible, clearly identifiable, and positioned above the registration form fields (e.g., name, email, password inputs) on the sign up screen

tests.scenario: Exclusive platform logo is missing or not rendered on the sign up screen
steps: Open a supported web browser
Navigate to the Exclusive platform sign up URL
Simulate a broken image or blocked asset by disabling image loading in the browser settings or intercepting the logo asset request to return a 404 error
Reload the sign up page and observe the logo area
tests.expected_result: The logo area should display an appropriate fallback (e.g., alt text 'Exclusive') and the broken image should not be silently hidden; the layout should still position the logo placeholder above the registration form, indicating the logo element is present in the DOM even if the asset fails to load

tests.scenario: Exclusive platform logo remains prominently displayed above the registration form at the minimum supported viewport width
steps: Open a supported web browser
Navigate to the Exclusive platform sign up URL
Resize the browser viewport to the minimum supported width (e.g., 320px wide) using developer tools or a responsive design testing tool
Observe the position and visibility of the Exclusive platform logo relative to the registration form
tests.expected_result: At the minimum supported viewport width, the Exclusive platform logo is still fully visible, not cropped or hidden, and remains positioned above the registration form without overlapping or being pushed below any form elements

tests.scenario: Sign up page displays a prominent heading at the top of the registration form
steps: Launch the Exclusive platform in a supported web browser
Navigate to the Sign Up or Registration page
Observe the top section of the registration form
tests.expected_result: A prominent heading such as 'Create Account' or 'Sign Up' is clearly visible at the top of the registration form, rendered with a larger or bold font style that distinguishes it from other page elements

tests.scenario: Sign up page is missing the required heading above the registration form
steps: Launch the Exclusive platform in a supported web browser
Navigate to the Sign Up or Registration page
Inspect the top section of the registration form for any heading element (e.g., h1, h2, or equivalent)
Check whether the heading text matches expected values such as 'Create Account' or 'Sign Up'
tests.expected_result: If the heading is absent, incorrectly labeled (e.g., 'Login' or 'Welcome'), or not positioned at the top of the form, the test should fail, indicating a violation of AC-10 that must be resolved before release

tests.scenario: Sign up heading text is at the exact character boundary of acceptable label variations
steps: Launch the Exclusive platform in a supported web browser
Navigate to the Sign Up or Registration page
Inspect the heading element at the top of the registration form and capture its exact text content
Verify the heading text matches one of the accepted boundary values: the shortest acceptable label 'Sign Up' (7 characters) and the longest acceptable label 'Create Account' (14 characters)
Confirm no truncation, overflow, or wrapping occurs for either label at standard desktop and mobile viewport sizes
tests.expected_result: The heading displays fully and correctly for both the shortest accepted value 'Sign Up' and the longest accepted value 'Create Account' without truncation or layout breakage, and any text outside these accepted values is not rendered as the page heading

tests.scenario: Verify that the descriptive subheading 'Enter your details below' is displayed beneath the main heading on the Sign Up screen
steps: Open a supported web browser and navigate to the Exclusive platform URL
Locate and click the 'Sign Up' link or button on the homepage or login page
Observe the Sign Up screen layout, specifically the area beneath the main heading
